tunings.name: Nashville (high strung)
tunings.note: The four low strings an octave up, from a 12-string set

tunings.name: Standard
tunings.note: The four low pairs have an octave string; the B and E pairs are two strings at the same pitch

tunings.name: Russian (7-string)
tunings.note: Open G, the Russian guitar's own tuning

tunings.name: E9
tunings.note: Strings 10 to 1, open (no pedals)

tunings.name: C6
tunings.note: Strings 10 to 1, open (no pedals)

tunings.name: Solo tuning
tunings.note: A whole step up, for solo playing with solo strings

tunings.name: Standard
tunings.note: Re-entrant: the 5th and 6th strings drop back down

tunings.name: Standard
tunings.note: About an octave below a 12-string: the three low pairs have an octave string, the top three are pairs at the same pitch

tunings.name: Standard (high G)
tunings.note: Re-entrant: the G string is higher than the C

tunings.name: Standard
tunings.note: Four pairs, both strings of a pair at the same pitch

tunings.name: Octave strings on the low pairs
Open G
tunings.note: The short 5th string comes first

tunings.name: Baroque (A = 415)
tunings.note: Set the reference to 415 Hz

tunings.name: Standard (ADAE)
tunings.note: The 4 melody strings, then the 5 sympathetic strings under them (a common setup; it changes with the piece)

tunings.name: Standard
tunings.note: The 4 played strings; tune the sympathetic strings by ear

tunings.name: In G
tunings.note: Single top string; octave strings on the three low pairs (the 4th is sometimes at the same pitch)

tunings.name: In G
tunings.note: Single top string; octave strings on the five low pairs

tunings.name: D minor
tunings.note: Two single top strings, octave strings on the eight basses; the basses are often retuned to the key of the piece

tunings.name: Standard
tunings.note: Single top string, the others in pairs

tunings.name: Re-entrant (Spanish)
tunings.note: No low strings: the 4th and 5th pairs are tuned high

tunings.name: G/C
tunings.note: Drones (bourdon C, mouche G, trompette C), then the two melody strings on G. Drone setups vary by maker

tunings.name: GDAD (octave low pairs)
tunings.note: Octave strings on the G and D pairs, a common setup

tunings.name: Arabic
tunings.note: Single low string, then five pairs

tunings.name: Standard
tunings.note: Re-entrant: the middle pair has the lowest string, an octave under its partner

tunings.name: Standard
tunings.note: Re-entrant: the 1st string is lower than the 2nd

tunings.name: Standard
tunings.note: Octave strings on the B and E pairs

tunings.name: Standard (C)
tunings.note: Octave strings on the G and E pairs

tunings.name: Standard
tunings.note: Three groups of three strings

tunings.name: Standard
tunings.note: Re-entrant

tunings.name: Modern
tunings.note: Three groups of three: the middle string of the low three groups is an octave down

tunings.name: Honchoshi
tunings.note: Usually tuned to the singer: move it all up or down together

tunings.name: Concert pitch
tunings.note: Shows the note you read

tunings.name: Concert pitch (sounds an octave up)
tunings.note: Shows the note you read

tunings.name: Any note
tunings.note: Voice, piano, harp, drums, handpan, didgeridoo, bagpipes...
